page.layout: One page of text, a single block of verse set in long lines, with no margin notes. Below the verse, the catchword "GRA-" stands at the right.

p.i: Quos summus olim quum veniet Polo Flammante Iudex plectet atrox scelus. Sed lucis alma quos Iubar excutit, Altelte cœci nubila pectoris, Non tristis illos vexat opum fames, Fallaxue honorum spes cruciat, neque Blandis Voluptas illecebris trahit: Non corda fœdo crimine taminant, Non rem maligna fraude suam expetunt Augere, limo non oculo inuidi Vicina messes prædia reddere Opimiores, & melioribus Replere cernunt fructibus horrea. Non plura poscunt quàm super i manus Benigna Patris porrigit in diem, Viuunt quieti nec metuunt sua Si fila Parca præcipites secant, Quum Christus illis vinere cognitus Det dulce, donec vile colunt lutum. Et donet idem dulcius emori, Quum vera puris præmia cœtibus Et lucra tendit sedibus æthereis Qua nec rubigo, nec timea vorax Morsus, nec audens diripiat Latro.

main_text.p: Lines printed in italics. Not transcribed in full detail: see notes.

page.notes: Several words in the verse are doubtful and not marked with [?] in every case: "Altelte" (line 4), "vinere" (line 18), "æthereis" (line 22) and "timea" (line 23) are uncertain readings. The ligature-like sign before "eniet" in line 1 and the sign before "ile" in line 19 are unclear. The line "super i manus" (line 14) has a doubtful word break. The page has no running head or page number. The catchword GRA- is the start of the next word on the following page.
